title: Definition
body_md:
Let \(\mathscr T_X\) denote the \(\Sigma_2\)-theory of \(V\) with parameters in
    \(\textnormal{Ord}\cup \{X\}\). 
    Let \(\mathscr H_X\) denote the structure \((\textnormal{HOD}_X,\mathscr T_X,{\in})\).
    Also let \(\mathscr T = \mathscr T_\emptyset\) and \(\mathscr H = \mathscr H_\emptyset\).

label: prp:hod-realization
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prp:hod-realization}
    Suppose \(X\) is a set, \(H\) is a countable transitive structure, and \[\rho : H\to \mathscr H_X\] is an elementary embedding. Then there is a countable transitive model \(\bar V\) of \(\textnormal{ZF}\)
    and a set \(\bar X\in \bar V\)
    such that \(H = (\mathscr H_{\bar X})^{\bar V}\).
    Thus \(\rho\) is partial elementary from \((\bar V,\bar X)\) to \((V,X)\).

label: thm:derived
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:derived}
    Assume \(\textnormal{AD}^+ + V = L(P(\mathbb R))\). 
    There is a definable inner model \(M\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}\) with a limit of Woodin cardinals \(\eta\)
    and a generic elementary embedding \[j : V\to D\]
    where \(D\) is a derived model of \(M\) at \(\eta\).

label: thm:ua
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:ua}
    Assume \(\textnormal{AD}^+ + V = L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\). Then
    \(\mathscr H\) satisfies weak comparison:
    if \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) are finitely generated
    structures 
    elementarily embeddable into \(\mathscr H\),
    then either \(H_0\in H_1\), \(H_1\in H_0\),
    or there are close embeddings
    \(k_0 : H_0 \to H^*\) and \(k_1 : H_1\to H^*\).

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(M\) and \(\eta\)
    be as in \cref{thm:derived}, and let \(\mathbb R^* = \mathbb R \cap M\).

    Suppose that \(H\in \mathscr H\) is a countable transitive structure that
    is elementarily embeddable into \(\mathscr H\).\footnote{
        Throughout this section, we work in choiceless Morse--Kelley set theory, 
        which allows us to refer to the first-order satisfaction predicate of \(V\).
        With a bit more work, the proofs can be carried out in \(\textnormal{ZF}\).
    } 
    We begin by constructing a 
    close elementary embedding
    \(k : H \to H^*\) where \(H^*\) is \(\mathscr H^{D^*}\) 
    for a model \(D^*\) of the form \(L_\alpha(\mathbb R^*,\Gamma)\)
    with \(\Gamma\) an initial segment of \(\textnormal{Hom}_{<\eta}^{M}\).

    By \cref{prp:hod-realization}, choose a countable transitive model
    \(\bar V\equiv V\) such that \(\mathscr H^{\bar V}=H\).
    Applying \cref{thm:derived} inside \(\bar V\), let
    \(\bar M\subseteq H\), \(\bar\eta\), and the generic elementary embedding
    \(j : \bar V\to D\) be as in that theorem, where
    \(D\) is a derived model of \(\bar M\) at \(\bar\eta\).
    Define \[i : H\to\mathscr H^D\]
    by \(i = j\restriction H\).
    By the observations following \cref{thm:derived}, \(i\) is definable over \(H\).

    Note that \(\bar M\in M\) and by absoluteness,
    \(M\) sees that \(\bar M\) is elementarily embeddable into \(M\).
    Therefore using Neeman-style \(\mathbb R\)-genericity iterations,\footnote{
        Woodin's original construction used Woodin-style genericity iterations,
        which requires establishing certain instances of the unique branch hypothesis.
        Steel suggested replacing them with Neeman-style iterations using \cite{Steel}.
    } we can iterate \((\bar M,\bar\eta)\) 
    to a model \((M^*,\eta^*)\), again elementarily embeddable into \(M\),
    such that \(\mathbb R^* = \mathbb R\cap M\) are the reals of a symmetric collapse of \(M^*\) at
    \(\eta^*\), and if \(D^*\) is the derived model of \(M^*\) at \(\eta^*\) in \({M}^*(\mathbb R^*)\), then
    \(\Gamma = \textnormal{Hom}^{D^*}\) is an initial segment of 
    \(\textnormal{Hom}_{<\eta}^{M}\).

    Let \[\pi : \bar M \to {M}^*\] be the iteration map.
    Then \(\pi\restriction {\mathscr{H}}^D\) is elementary from
    \({\mathscr{H}}^D\) to \({\mathscr{H}}^{D^*}\).
    Set \(H^* = {\mathscr{H}}^{D^*}\). Define an elementary embedding \(k : H \to H^*\)
    by \[k = \pi \circ i\] 

    We claim that \(k\) is close to \(H\). 
    To prove this, fix \(A\in H^*\), and let us show that
    \(k^{-1}[A] \in H\). We have 
    \(\pi^{-1}[A]\in \bar M\) since \(\pi\) is close to \(\bar M\) and \(A\in M^*\).
    Since \(\bar M\subseteq H\), it follows that \(\pi^{-1}[A]\in H\) and hence \(i^{-1}[\pi^{-1}[A]]\in H\) since \(i\) is definable over \(H\). But \(k^{-1}[A] = i^{-1}[\pi^{-1}[A]]\).
    
    We will use that \[D^* = \textnormal{Hull}^{D^*}(k[H]\cup\Lambda)\]
    where \(\Lambda = P(\mathbb R)\cap D^*\).
    This follows from the fact that \(H^* = \textnormal{Hull}^{H^*}(k[H]\cup k(\Theta^H))\),
    which holds because \(k\) is close to \(H\)
    and every uniform measure of \(H\) lies on a cardinal less than
    or equal to \(\Theta^H\).

    We now show that Weak Comparison holds for \({\mathscr{H}}\).
    Fix any two
    finitely generated models \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) that are elementarily embeddable into \({\mathscr{H}}\). We will construct close embeddings \(k_0 : H_0 \to H^*_0\) and \(k_1 : H_1\to H^*_1\)
    such that \(H^*_0\) and \(H_1^*\) are \textit{comparable}: either they are equal or one belongs to the other.

    For \(\ell = 0,1\), the construction above yields
    a close embedding \(k_\ell : H_\ell\to H_\ell^*\) where \(H_\ell^* =  {\mathscr{H}}^{D_\ell^*}\) for
    a model \(D_\ell^*\) satisfying 
    \(\mathbb R\cap D_\ell^* = \mathbb R\cap M\), \(\Gamma_\ell = \textnormal{Hom}^{D_\ell^*}\lhd \textnormal{Hom}_{<\eta}^{M}\),
    and \(D_\ell^* = \textnormal{Hull}^{D_\ell^*}(k_\ell[H_\ell]\cup \Lambda_\ell)\)
    where \(\Lambda_\ell = P(\mathbb R^*)\cap D_\ell^*\).

    We claim that \(D_0^*\) and \(D_1^*\) are comparable. 
    By Wadge determinacy in \(\textnormal{Hom}_{<\eta}^{M}\), \(\Gamma_0\) and \(\Gamma_1\) are comparable pointclasses. It follows from our assumption that \(V = L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\)
    that \(\Lambda_0\) and \(\Lambda_1\) are comparable as well.
    (If \(\Gamma_0 = \Gamma_1\), this is trivial, and if \(\Gamma_0 \lhd \Gamma_1\),
    then \(\Gamma_0^\#\in D_1^*\), so \(\Lambda_0\lhd \Lambda_1\).)
    By symmetry, it suffices to show that if \(\Lambda_0 \lhd \Lambda_1\), then \(D_0^*\in D_1^*\). 

    Suppose first that every set of reals has a sharp. 
    We will use that \(D_1^*\) is correct about
    sharps, which means that if \(A\in D_1^*\) and \(D_1^*\vDash B = A^\#\), then 
    in fact, \(B = A^\#\). 
    To see this, note that \(M_1^*\) is correct about sharps
    because \(M_1^*\) is elementarily embeddable into \(M\).
    It follows that \(D_1^*\) is correct about
    sharps, since  \(D_1^*\) is an inner model of a forcing extension of \(M_1^*\).

    Since \(D_{0}^* = \textnormal{Hull}^{D_0^*}(k_0[H_0]\cup\Lambda_0)\) and \(H_0\) is finitely generated, \(D_0^*\) is coded by a subset of \(\Lambda_0\) in \(L(\mathbb R^*,\Lambda_0)\). 
    Since \(\Lambda_0^\#\in D_1^*\), \(D_0^*\in D_1^*\). 

    Suppose instead that some set of reals has no sharp. 
    We then have that \(\theta = \Theta^{H_0}\) is regular in \(H_0\). It follows that
    \(k_0(\theta) = \sup k_0[\theta]\) since \(\theta\) carries no uniform measures in \(H_0\) and \(k_0\) is close to \(H_0\). 
    In particular, \(\textnormal{cf}^{M}(k_0(\theta)) = \omega\).
    (We use that \(k_0\in M\), which follows from the fact that \(H_0^*\in M\) 
    and \(H_0\) is finitely
    generated.) Therefore \(D_{0}^* = \textnormal{Hull}^{D_0^*}(\mathbb R^*\cup \mathcal A)\) where 
    \(\mathcal A = \{a_n : n < \omega\}\) 
    is a countable set in \(M\). Letting \(T_n = \text{Th}^{D_0^*}_{\Sigma_n}(\mathbb R^*\cup \{a_0,\dots,a_{n-1}\})\), we have \(\{T_n\}_{n < \omega}\subseteq D_0^*\) and \(\langle T_n\rangle_{n < \omega}\in M\), and hence \(\langle T_n\rangle_{n < \omega}\in D_1^*\).
    Since \(D_0^*\) can be recovered from  \(\langle T_n\rangle_{n < \omega}\), it follows that
    \(D_0^* \in D_1^*\).

    Thus we have shown that \(D_0^*\) and \(D_1^*\) are comparable.
    If \(D_0^*\in D_1^*\), for example, then \(D_0^*\) is \(\textnormal{OD}\) in \(D_1^*\) and hence
    \(H_0^*\in H_1^*\). It follows that \(H_0^*\) and \(H_1^*\) are comparable, and
    this establishes weak comparison. (Note here that if \(H_0^*\in H_1^*\), then \(H_0\in H_1\).)

label: thm:woodin_strong
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:woodin_strong}
    Assume \(\textnormal{AD}^+ + V = L(P(\mathbb R))\) and \(\delta\) is the largest Suslin. If
    \(\lambda < \Theta\),
    there is a normal measure \(U\) on \(\delta\)
    with \(j_U(\delta) > \lambda\) and
    \(P(\lambda)\cap j_U(\textnormal{HOD}) = P(\lambda)\cap \textnormal{HOD}\).\qed

label: thm:spector
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:spector}
    Assume \(\textnormal{ZF} + \textnormal{DC} + V = L(X)\) for some set \(X\). 
    Then for any measure \(U\), in a forcing extension,
    there is an inner model \(M\), an elementary embedding \[j : V \to M\]
    and an embedding \(k : \textnormal{Ult}(V,U)\to M\)
    such that \(\textnormal{Ord}\subseteq \textnormal{ran}(k)\) and
    \(k\circ j_U = j\).

label: thm:ua_hod_s
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:ua_hod_s}
    Under \(\textnormal{AD}^+ + V = L(P(\mathbb R))\), 
    \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) satisfies \(\textnormal{UA}\) for every \(s \in\textnormal{Ord}^\omega\).
    \begin{proof}
        We first prove the theorem in the case that \(V = L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\).
        Let \(H\) be a pointwise definable transitive structure that is elementarily embeddable into \(\mathscr H\). 
        
        Fix a countable transitive model \(\bar V\equiv V\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}\), constructed by type omission, so that
        \(H = \mathscr H^{\bar V}\). 
        Fix \(s\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\cap \bar V\). We will show \(\textnormal{UA}\) holds in \(P = \mathscr H_s^{\bar V}\).

        Fix internal ultrapowers \(e_0 : P\to P_0\) and \(e_1 : P \to P_1\), and let \(s_n = e_n(s)\). For \(n = 0,1\), we imitate the construction from \cref{thm:ua}. That is, construct \(\bar V_n\equiv V\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}\) by relativizing \cref{prp:hod-realization} 
        so that
        \[P_n = \mathscr H_{s_n}^{\bar V_n}\]
        Applying \cref{thm:derived} in \(\bar V_n\), fix \(\bar M_n\subseteq \mathscr H^{\bar V_n}\), \(\bar\eta_n\), and an elementary \(j_n : \bar V_n\to D_n\) where \(D_n\) is a derived model of \(\bar M_n\) at \(\bar\eta_n\).
        Let \(t_n =j_n(s_n)\) and define
        \[
            i_n : P_n\to\mathscr H^{D_n}_{t_n}
        \]
        by \(i_n = j_n\restriction P_n\).

        By \cref{thm:derived}, fix \(\gamma_n < \bar\eta_n\) such that \(t_n\) is
        \({<}\gamma_n\)-generic over \(\bar M_n\).
        Let \(\pi_n : \bar M_n\to M_n^*\) be a Neeman-style \(\mathbb R^*\)-genericity iteration above \(\gamma_n\), where \(\mathbb R^* = \mathbb R\cap \textnormal{HOD}\), such that if \(D_n^*\) is the derived model of \(M_n^*\) as computed in \(M_n^*(\mathbb R^*)\),
        then \(D_0^*\) and \(D_1^*\) are comparable.
        Let \(s_n^* = \pi_n[t_n]\), and let
        \[
            \pi_n^+ : \bar M_n[t_n]\to M_n^*[s_n^*]
        \]
        be the unique extension coming from L\'evy--Solovay.
        Finally let \(k_n = \pi_n^+\circ i_n\), so
        \[
            k_n : P_n\to \mathscr H_{s_n^*}^{D_n^*}
        \]
        is a close embedding.

        We first show that \(D_0^* = D_1^*\).
        We have elementary embeddings
        \begin{align*}
            (k_0\circ e_0)\restriction H : H\to \mathscr H^{D_0^*}\\ 
            (k_1\circ e_1)\restriction H : H \to \mathscr H^{D_1^*}
        \end{align*}
        Assuming towards a contradiction that 
        \(D_0^* \in D_1^*\), for example, we would have
        that \(H\) is coded by a real in \(\mathscr H^{D_1^*}\).
        Since \(\textnormal{crit}(k_1\circ e_1) > (2^{\aleph_0})^H\),
        \(H\) and \(\mathscr H^{D_1^*}\) have the same reals,
        and so \(H\) is coded by a real in \(H\), which is a contradiction. This proves that \(D_0^* = D_1^*\),
        so let us denote this model by \(D^*\).

        Since \(H\) is pointwise definable, it follows that
        \(k_0\circ e_0 \restriction H = k_1\circ e_1\restriction H\).
        Therefore
        \(k_0\circ e_0[s] = k_1\circ e_1[s]\),
        and hence \(k_0\circ e_0(s) = k_1\circ e_1(s)\).
        In other words, \(k_0(s_0) = k_1(s_1)\), and so
        \(\mathscr H_{k_0(s_0)}^{D^*} = \mathscr H_{k_1(s_1)}^{D^*}\).
        Now \(k_0\circ e_0\) and \(k_1\circ e_1\) have the same target model, and
        since every element of \(P = \mathscr H_s^{\bar V}\) is definable in \(P\)
        from \(s\), 
        and \(k_0\circ e_0(s) = k_1\circ e_1(s)\), 
        we obtain \(k_0\circ e_0 = k_1\circ e_1\). This yields \(\textnormal{UA}\) for \(e_0\) and \(e_1\), as desired.

        Now assume \(V \neq L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\).
        Let \(\delta\) be the largest Suslin cardinal. 
        We will show that 
        for all \(s\in \Theta^\omega\), \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) satisfies \(\textnormal{UA}\). This suffices for the result: if \(t\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\), then since \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\) is a \(\Theta\)-cc extension of \(\textnormal{HOD}\), there is a set \(S\in \textnormal{HOD}\) such that \(\textnormal{ot}(S) < \Theta\) and \(\textnormal{ran}(t)\subseteq S\), and therefore \(\textnormal{HOD}_t = \textnormal{HOD}_s\) for some \(s\in \Theta^\omega\).

        Let \(\delta\) be the largest Suslin cardinal, which exists since
        \(\textnormal{Hom}\neq P(\mathbb R)\). 
        By Suslin-co-Suslin reflection, \(\textnormal{Hom} = \textnormal{Hom}^{L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})}\)
        and for all \(s\in \delta^\omega\), \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\delta = \textnormal{HOD}^{L(\mathbb R, \textnormal{Hom})}_s\cap V_\delta \).
        Thus, \(L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\) satisfies \(\textnormal{AD}^+ + V = L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\),
        so by the previous case, \(\textnormal{UA}\) holds in \(\textnormal{HOD}^{L(\mathbb R, \textnormal{Hom})}_s\) for all \(s\in \delta^\omega\).
        In the context of \(\textnormal{ZFC}\), since \(\textnormal{UA}\) is a \(\Pi_2\)-sentence, 
        \(\textnormal{UA}\) is downwards absolute to any 
        \(V_\rho\) with \(|V_\rho| = \rho\).
        Thus for all \(s\in \delta^\omega\),
        \(\textnormal{UA}\) holds in \[\textnormal{HOD}^{L(\mathbb R, \textnormal{Hom})}_s\cap V_\delta = \textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\delta\]

        Assume towards a contradiction that \(\textnormal{UA}\) fails in 
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) for some \(s\in\Theta^\omega\). 
        Fix a limit ordinal \(\gamma < \Theta\) such that \(\sup(s) < \gamma\) and \(\textnormal{UA}\) fails in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma\).
        We claim there is some \(\lambda < \Theta\) large enough that
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma \subseteq (\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\).
        For this, note that every bounded subset of \(\Theta\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has a \(\mathbb B\)-name in \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\Theta\) where \(\mathbb B\) is the \(\infty\)-Borel Vop\v{e}nka algebra adding an element of \(\gamma^\omega\) to \(\textnormal{HOD}\). 
        This is by a nice name argument, using that 
        \(\mathbb B\) is \(\Theta\)-cc in \(\textnormal{HOD}\)
        and \(\mathbb B\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\Theta\). 
        Now let \(S\) be a bounded subset of \(\Theta\) coding \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma\), and fix \(\lambda < \Theta\) large enough that this set has a \(\mathbb B\)-name \(\dot S\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda\). Then
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma \subseteq (\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\),
        since \(\dot S\) can be interpreted  
        in \((\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\).
       
        Let \(j : V\to M\) be a Spector ultrapower by a \(\delta\)-complete measure on \(\delta\) such that
        \(j(\delta) > \lambda\), \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\cap V_\lambda = \textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda\). Note that \(\textnormal{Ord}^\omega\cap V\subseteq M\) by countable choice, and in particular \(s\in M\). 
        Since all measures on ordinals are \(\textnormal{OD}\),
        \(\textnormal{HOD}^M_s \subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_s\). On the other hand,
        \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}^M_s\), so \[\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma\subseteq (\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}^M_s\] 
        It follows that \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma = \textnormal{HOD}^M_s\cap V_\gamma\). Therefore \(\textnormal{UA}\) fails in \(\textnormal{HOD}^M_s\cap V_\gamma\), and hence it fails in \(\textnormal{HOD}^M_s\cap V_{j(\delta)}\),
        contradicting that in \(V\),
        \(\textnormal{UA}\) holds in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\delta\)
        for any \(s\in \delta^\omega\).
    \end{proof}

        For this, note that every bounded subset of \(\Theta\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has a \(\mathbb B\)-name in \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\Theta\) where \(\mathbb B\) is the \(\infty\)-Borel Vop\v{e}nka algebra adding an element of \(\gamma^\omega\) to \(\textnormal{HOD}\). 
        This is by a nice name argument, using that 
        \(\mathbb B\) is \(\Theta\)-cc in \(\textnormal{HOD}\)
        and \(\mathbb B\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\Theta\). 
        Now let \(S\) be a bounded subset of \(\Theta\) coding \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma\), and fix \(\lambda < \Theta\) large enough that this set has a \(\mathbb B\)-name \(\dot S\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda\). Then
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma \subseteq (\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\),
        since \(\dot S\) can be interpreted  
        in \((\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\).
       
        Let \(j : V\to M\) be a Spector ultrapower by a \(\delta\)-complete measure on \(\delta\) such that
        \(j(\delta) > \lambda\), \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\cap V_\lambda = \textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda\). Note that \(\textnormal{Ord}^\omega\cap V\subseteq M\) by countable choice, and in particular \(s\in M\). 
        Since all measures on ordinals are \(\textnormal{OD}\),
        \(\textnormal{HOD}^M_s \subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_s\). On the other hand,
        \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}^M_s\), so \[\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma\subseteq (\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\lambda)[s]\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}^M_s\] 
        It follows that \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\gamma = \textnormal{HOD}^M_s\cap V_\gamma\). Therefore \(\textnormal{UA}\) fails in \(\textnormal{HOD}^M_s\cap V_\gamma\), and hence it fails in \(\textnormal{HOD}^M_s\cap V_{j(\delta)}\),
        contradicting that in \(V\),
        \(\textnormal{UA}\) holds in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\delta\)
        for any \(s\in \delta^\omega\).

title: Proof
body_md:
We can reduce to the case that \(V = L(\mathbb R,\textnormal{Hom})\)
    by essentially the same argument from \cref{thm:ua_hod_s}.

    Suppose \(H\) is the pointwise definable hull of \(\mathscr H\).
    By \cref{prp:hod-realization}, we can form a model \(\bar V\equiv V\)
    such that \(H = \mathscr H^{\bar V}\). 
    Fix \(s\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\cap \bar V\), and suppose \(e : H_s \to H_1\) is the ultrapower of \(H_s = (\mathscr H_s)^{\bar V}\) by a measure \(U\in H_s\).
    It suffices to show that
    \(U\) extends to a countably complete filter in \(\bar V\).
    Fix \(\sigma \in (P_{\omega_1}(U))^{\bar V}\). We will show that
    \(\bigcap \sigma\neq \emptyset\).

    We use the construction from the proof of \cref{thm:ua_hod_s},
    with \(M\) and \(\eta\) as in \cref{thm:derived} and
    \(\mathbb R^*=\mathbb R\cap M\).
    Applying \cref{thm:derived} inside \(\bar V\), let
    \(\bar M\subseteq H\), \(\bar\eta\), and the generic elementary embedding
    \(j:\bar V\to D\) be as in that theorem, where
    \(D\) is a derived model of \(\bar M\) at \(\bar\eta\). 
    Since \(j(\sigma)\) and \(j(s)\) are in \(D\), they belong to a common
    \({<}\bar\eta\)-generic extension of \(\bar M\).
    Thus by taking the critical point of the genericity iteration
    \(\pi : \bar M \to M^*\) sufficiently large, we can ensure that
    \(\pi\) lifts uniquely to an elementary embedding
    \(\pi^+\) of
    \(\bar M[j(\sigma),j(s)]\).
    As in \cref{thm:ua_hod_s}, let \(k = \pi^+\circ j\restriction H_s\).

    Let \(Q = \mathscr H_{k(s)}^{D^*}\) be the target model of \(k\).
    The construction from \cref{thm:ua_hod_s} yields \(k_1 : H_1\to Q\) such that
    \(k = k_1\circ e\).
    
    Let \(a = [\textnormal{id}]_U\). Then \(a\in \bigcap e[\sigma]\),
    so \(k_1(a)\in \bigcap (k_1\circ e)[\sigma] =  \bigcap k[\sigma]\). 
    In particular, \(\bigcap k[\sigma]\neq \emptyset\), and 
    since \(k[\sigma] = \pi^+(j[\sigma])\), it follows that
    \(\bigcap j[\sigma]\neq \emptyset\).
    Finally, the elementarity of
    \(j:\bar V\to D\) implies \(\bigcap\sigma\neq\emptyset\).

label: lma:ad_weakly_normal
title: Lemma
body_md:
Assume \(\textnormal{AD} + \textnormal{DC}_\mathbb R\).\label{lma:ad_weakly_normal}
    Every ordinal \(\delta < \Theta\) of uncountable cofinality 
    carries a weakly normal measure that concentrates 
    on \(S^\delta_\omega\).
    \begin{proof}
        Let \(W\) be a Ketonen minimal measure
        extending the tail filter on \(\delta\).
        If \(f : \delta\to \delta\) is regressive on a \(W\)-large set,
        then \(f_*(W) <_{\Bbbk} W\), and so \(f_*(W)\) is not uniform, which means that
        \(f_*(W)\) concentrates on a bounded set; in other words, \(f\) is bounded on a \(W\)-large set.
        This proves \(W\) is weakly normal.

        If \(S^\delta_\omega\notin W\), let \(S = \delta\setminus S^\delta_\omega\). 
        For each \(\alpha\in S\), choose
        \(U_\alpha\in \textnormal{meas}(\alpha)\) extending the tail filter on \(\alpha\).
        (Recall Kunen's theorem that the measures are well-ordered.)
        Put \(A\in U\) if and only if \(\{\alpha\in S : A\cap \alpha\in U_\alpha\}\in W\).
        Then \(U<_{\Bbbk} W\), but clearly \(U\) extends the tail filter, contrary to the minimality
        of \(W\).
    \end{proof}

label: lma:ketonen
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lma:ketonen}
    Suppose \(s\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\), \(\kappa\) is a cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), and \(\eta\in(\kappa,\Theta)\) is regular in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\). If \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa)\)-cover property at \(\eta\), then \((\kappa_{\mathscr K_\eta})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} \leq \kappa\).
    \begin{proof}
        The \((\aleph_1,\kappa)\)-cover property at \(\eta\) implies \(\eta\) has uncountable cofinality, and hence \(\mathscr K^s_\eta\) exists. 
        Note that \(S^\eta_\omega \in \mathscr K_\eta^s\) by \cref{lma:min_weakly_normal}: by the ordinal definability of measures, if \(\alpha < \Theta\) and \(\textnormal{cf}^{\textnormal{HOD}_s}(\alpha)\) carries no uniform measure in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), then \(\textnormal{cf}(\alpha) = \omega\).
        The \((\aleph_1,\kappa)\)-cover property then implies
        \((S^\eta_{<\kappa})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} \in \mathscr K_\eta^s\).
        
        Now let \(j : \textnormal{HOD}_s\to M\) be the ultrapower embedding associated to \(\mathscr K_\eta^s\).
        We must show \(\textnormal{crit}(j)\leq \kappa\). By \L o\'s's theorem, \([\textnormal{id}]_{\mathscr K^s_\eta} \in \left(S^{j(\eta)}_{<j(\kappa)}\right)^{M}\), or in other words:
        \[\textnormal{cf}^M(\sup j[\eta]) < j(\kappa)\]
        Since \(\textnormal{cf}^{\textnormal{HOD}_s}(\sup j[\eta]) = \eta\),
        we must have \(j(\kappa) \geq \eta\), and hence \(\textnormal{crit}(j)\leq \kappa\).
    \end{proof}

body_md:
\label{lma:seminormal}
    For all sequences \(s\in I_\xi\), \(\delta\) carries distinct seminormal measures
    in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).
    \begin{proof}
        Since \(\xi\) is a strong limit cardinal in \(N^+\), 
        \((2^\delta)^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} < \xi\). 
        In particular, every \(\omega\)-sequence of \(\textnormal{OD}_s\)-subsets of \(\delta\)
        belongs to \(N\).
        Let 
        \(S_0 = S^\delta_\omega\) and \(S_1 = \delta \setminus S_0\);
        since \(\delta\geq \omega_2\), both are stationary in \(N\).
        Let \(F\) be the club filter of \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) and let \(F_0 = F|S_0\) and \(F_1 = F|S_1\). 
        Then \(F_0\) and \(F_1\) extend to countably complete filters
        in \(V\), and thus extend to measures \(U_0\) and \(U_1\) in \(V\).
        By Kunen's theorem, these measures are \(\textnormal{OD}\),
        and therefore \(U_0\cap \textnormal{HOD}_s\) and \(U_1\cap \textnormal{HOD}_s\) witness
        that in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), there are distinct seminormal measures
        on \(\delta\).
    \end{proof}

label: prp:gamma_kappa_cov
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prp:gamma_kappa_cov}
    Suppose \(s\in I_\xi\), 
    \(\bar \kappa = (\kappa_{\mathscr K_\delta^s})^{N}\), and
    \(\kappa = (\kappa_{\mathscr K_\delta^s})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s}\).
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \((\bar \kappa,\kappa)\)-cover property at
         \(\delta\) in \(N\).
        \item \(\mathscr K_\delta^s\) witnesses that \(\kappa\) is \(\delta\)-strongly compact
        and \({<}\delta\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).
        \item \(\kappa\) is \(\delta\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).
    \end{enumerate}
    \begin{proof}
        Since \(\delta\) carries distinct seminormal measures, 
        we can apply \cref{thm:supercompact} 
        to conclude that \(\mathscr K_\delta^s\) witnesses that \(\kappa\) is \(\delta\)-strongly compact
        and \({<}\delta\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\),
        and moreover \(\kappa\) is \(\delta\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).
        Since \(\mathscr K_\delta^s\) witnesses that \(\kappa\) is \(\delta\)-strongly compact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), there is a function \(p : \delta\to P_\kappa(\delta)\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\)
        such that \(\mathcal U = p_*(\mathscr K_\delta^s)\) is a fine measure on \(P_\kappa(\delta)\).

        The \((\bar \kappa,\kappa)\)-cover property now follows.
        Fix \(\sigma \in P_{\bar \kappa}(\delta)\cap N\).
        For \(\alpha < \delta\), define
        \[A_\alpha = \left\{\tau\in \left(P_\kappa(\delta)\right)^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} : \alpha\in \tau\right\}\]
        so \(A_\alpha\in \mathcal U\) by fineness.
        Since \(\mathscr K_\delta^s\) is \(\bar \kappa\)-complete,
        \(\bigcap_{\alpha\in \sigma}A_\alpha\neq \emptyset\),
        and if \(\tau\) belongs to this intersection, then \(\tau\in \textnormal{HOD}_s\), 
        \(\sigma\subseteq \tau\)
        and \(|\tau|^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} < \kappa\).
    \end{proof}

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prp:kappa_cov}
    Let \(\kappa = \kappa_\delta\), and suppose \(s\in I_\xi\) is such that \((\kappa_{\mathscr K^s_\delta})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} = \kappa\). Then
    \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \(\kappa\)-cover and approximation properties at \(\delta\) in \(N\). Moreover, 
    every \(S\in P(\delta)\cap N\) is in
    \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) for some \(x\in P(\kappa)\cap N\).
    \begin{proof}
        The \(\kappa\)-cover property
        follows immediately from \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov}.
        For the approximation property, 
        fix \(\mathcal A = \langle A_\alpha : \alpha < \delta\rangle\in \textnormal{HOD}_s\) such that
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) satisfies that \(\mathcal A\) is a \(\kappa\)-independent family 
        of subsets of \(\delta\). 
        Suppose \(T\in P(\delta)\cap N\) is \(\kappa\)-approximated by \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).
        Then the basis
        \[\mathcal B = \{A_\alpha : \alpha \in T\} \cup \{\delta\setminus A_\alpha : \alpha\notin T\}\]
        extends to a 
        \(\kappa\)-complete filter \(F\) in \(N\). 
        In particular, \(F\) 
        is countably complete in \(V\), and thus \(F\) extends to a measure \(U\) in \(V\).
        By Kunen's theorem, \(U\) is \(\textnormal{OD}\), and so \(U\cap \textnormal{HOD}_s\in \textnormal{HOD}_s\).
        Thus
        \(T = \{\alpha < \delta : A_\alpha\in U\}\in \textnormal{HOD}_s\).

        To show every \(S\in P(\delta)\cap N\) is in
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) for some \(x\in P(\kappa)\cap N\),
        fix \(t\in I_\xi\) such that \(s\) and \(S\) belong to \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\).
        Since \(\mathscr K^s_\delta\subseteq \mathscr K^t_\delta\),
        \((\kappa_{\mathscr K^t_\delta})^{\textnormal{HOD}_t} = \kappa\).
        In particular, \(\kappa\) is \(\delta\)-strongly compact in 
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\). Let \(x\subseteq \kappa\) code a well-order of \(P_\kappa(\kappa)\cap \textnormal{HOD}_t\). 
        Note that the models \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) and \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\) compute \(P_\kappa(\delta)\) the same way:
        of course, \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_t\), and in the other direction,
        if \(\sigma\in (P_\kappa(\delta))^{\textnormal{HOD}_t}\), then \(\sigma\) is covered by \(\tau\in (P_\kappa(\delta))^{\textnormal{HOD}_s}\) by the \(\kappa\)-cover property, \(P(\tau)\cap \textnormal{HOD}_t\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) since \(P_\kappa(\kappa)\cap \textnormal{HOD}_t\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\). The same argument shows that
        \[(\delta^{<\kappa})^{\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}} \leq (\delta^{<\kappa})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s}\cdot (\kappa^{<\kappa})^{\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}} = \delta\cdot \kappa = \delta\]
        
        This cardinal arithmetic yields \(\mathcal A = \langle A_\alpha : \alpha < \delta\rangle\in \textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) such that
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) satisfies that \(\mathcal A\) is a \(\kappa\)-independent family

\label{thm:monotonicity}
   If \(\delta_0 \leq \delta_1 < \xi\) are regular cardinals in \(N\), then \(\kappa_{\delta_0}\leq \kappa_{\delta_1}\).
    \begin{proof}
        By the Steel--Woodin theorem \cite[Theorem 2.18]{SteelOrdinalDefinability}, we may assume \(\delta_0 \geq \Theta^{N}\).
        By \cref{cor:ua_completeness},
        it suffices to show that for all \(s\in I_\xi\),
        \(\mathscr K_{\delta_1}^s\) is \(\kappa\)-complete in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) where
        \(\kappa = \kappa_{\delta_0}\). 

        Fix \(s\in I_\xi\). A consequence of \cite[Lemma 7.4.49]{UABook} is that under \(\textnormal{ZFC} + \textnormal{UA}\), if \(\gamma_0 \leq \gamma_1\) are regular non-isolated Fr\'echet cardinals, then \(\kappa_{\mathscr K_{\gamma_0}}\leq \kappa_{\mathscr K_{\gamma_1}}\).
        By \cref{lma:seminormal},
        both \(\delta_0\) and \(\delta_1\) carry distinct 
        seminormal measures in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), and so
        by \cite[Theorem 8.4.20]{UABook}, 
        they are regular non-isolated Fr\'echet cardinals in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).
        By \cref{prp:W_to_K}, it follows that
        \(\kappa \leq \kappa_{\mathscr K^s_{\delta_0}}\leq \kappa_{\mathscr K^s_{\delta_1}}\).
    \end{proof}

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
    Let \(\mathcal H = V_\xi^\textnormal{HOD}\). Inside \(N\), suppose \(\eta\) is a regular cardinal satisfying: 
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item \label{item:s_reflection} 
        For all \(\alpha < \eta\), \(P(\alpha) \subseteq \mathcal H({\eta^\omega})\). 
        \item \label{item:small_gen}  For all \(\alpha < \eta\), \(\Theta(\alpha^\omega)\leq \eta\).
    \end{enumerate}
    Then in \(N\), either \(\kappa_\eta = \eta\) or \(\mathcal H\) correctly computes all finite successors of \(\eta^{++}\).
    \begin{proof}
        By \ref{item:small_gen}, \(\Theta^{N} \leq \eta < \xi\),
        which puts us in a position to apply the previous results of this section 
        with \(\delta = \eta\).

        Assume towards a contradiction that the conclusion fails. 
        In other words, \(\kappa < \eta\) where \(\kappa = \kappa_\eta\).
        Fix \(s\in I_\xi\) such that \((\kappa_{\mathscr K_\eta^s})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} = \kappa\). 

        By \cref{prp:kappa_cov},
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the 
        \(\kappa\)-cover property at \(\delta\) in \(N\) and every \(S\in P(\eta)\cap N\) is in
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) for some \(x\in P(\kappa)\cap N\).
        Combining \ref{item:s_reflection} and \ref{item:small_gen}, for any \(x\in P(\kappa)\cap N\),
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) is an \(\eta\)-cc generic extension of \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\). Since every
        subset of \(\eta\) in \(N\) belongs to some such \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\), it follows that
        \((\eta^+)^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} = (\eta^+)^{N}\).

        Since \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has
        the \(\kappa\)-cover property at \(\eta\) and \((\eta^+)^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} = (\eta^+)^{N}\), 
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \(\kappa\)-cover property at \((\eta^+)^{N}\).
        Let \(\gamma = (\eta^+)^{N}\).
        Since \(\gamma\) is a cardinal in \(N\) that is 
        seen to be a successor cardinal by an inner model of choice,
        \(\gamma\) is regular in \(N\). 
        Applying \cref{lma:ketonen} and \cref{thm:monotonicity},
        \[\kappa = (\kappa_{\mathscr K^s_\eta})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} \leq (\kappa_{\mathscr K^s_\gamma})^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} \leq \kappa\] 
        Thus we can apply \cref{prp:kappa_cov}
        again, to obtain that every \(S\in P(\gamma)\cap N\) is in
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) for some \(x\in P(\kappa)\cap N\), and thus
        \((\gamma^+)^{\textnormal{HOD}_s} = (\gamma^+)^{N}\).

        Iterating this argument, we have that \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) correctly computes \((\eta^{+n})^{N}\)
        for all \(n < \omega\).
        Let \(\lambda = (\eta^{+\omega})^{N}\). 
        By \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov}, \(\kappa\) is \({<}\lambda\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) and
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \(\kappa\)-cover and approximation properties
        below \(\lambda\). Indeed, this holds in \(\textnormal{HOD}_{s,u}\) for all \(u\in I_\xi\).

        We claim that \(\Theta^{N}(P(\eta)) \leq (\gamma^+)^{N}\).
        Note first that since UA implies GCH in regions of supercompactness, 
        \((2^\eta)^{\textnormal{HOD}_{s,u}} = \gamma\) for all \(u\in I_\xi\).
        For each \(u\in \eta^\omega\), 
        let \(\langle S_\alpha^u : \alpha < \gamma\rangle\) be an \(\textnormal{OD}_{s,u}\)-enumeration of 
        \(P(\eta)\cap \textnormal{HOD}_{s,u}\). 
        Note that each \(S\subseteq \eta\) is of the form \(S_\alpha^u\) for some \(u\in \eta^\omega\)
        and \(\alpha < \gamma\),
        since \(S\in \textnormal{HOD}_{s,x}\) for some \(x\in P(\kappa)\cap N\) and
        \(x\in \textnormal{HOD}_u\) for some \(u\in \eta^\omega\) by \ref{item:s_reflection}.

        Suppose \(\nu < \Theta^{N}(P(\eta))\),
        and let us show \(\nu < (\gamma^+)^{N}\). 
        Suppose \(f : P(\eta)\to \nu\) is a surjection.
        Define \(g : \eta^\omega\times \gamma\to \nu\) by
        setting \(g(u,\alpha) = f(S^u_\alpha)\). Then \(g\) is also a surjection.
        Note however that for each fixed \(\alpha < \gamma\),
        if \(A_\alpha = \{g(u,\alpha) : u\in \eta^\omega\}\), then
        \(|A_\alpha|\leq \eta\) by \ref{item:small_gen}.
        (Here we use that \(\Theta^{N}(\eta^\omega) = ({\eta^+})^{N}\) as a consequence
        of \ref{item:small_gen}.)
        Since \(\nu = \bigcup_{\alpha < \gamma} A_\alpha\),
        \(\nu < (\gamma^+)^{N}\). 

        Fix \(y\subseteq \eta\) such that \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap P_\kappa(\eta)\) is
        coded by \(y\). 
        Since \(\Theta^{N}(P(\eta)) \leq (\gamma^+)^{N}\),
        \(\textnormal{HOD}_y\) is contained in a \((\gamma^+)^{N}\)-cc extension of
        \(\textnormal{HOD}\). Moreover, applying the Hamkins uniqueness theorem
        \cite[Theorem 4.7]{Goldberg2024StronglyCompactOD} at each finite successor of
        \(\eta\), we see that \(Y = P_\textnormal{bd}(\lambda)\cap \textnormal{HOD}_s\) is \(\textnormal{OD}_y\).
        In particular, \(\textnormal{HOD}_y^{L(Y)}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_y\). 
        Note that \(L(Y)\) is a model of \(\textnormal{ZFC} + \textnormal{UA}\) in which 
        \(\kappa\) is \({<}\lambda\)-supercompact; the fact that
        \(L(Y)\vDash \textnormal{AC}\) follows from \cite[Theorem 6.2.19]{UABook} applied in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), which implies that there is a well-order of \(Y\) that is definable from parameters over \(Y\).
        By \cite[Theorem 6.2.19]{UABook}, it follows that 
        \(Y\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_y^{L(Y)}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_y\).
        This implies that \(Y\) is contained in a \((\gamma^+)^{N}\)-cc extension
        of \(\textnormal{HOD}\). It follows that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) correctly computes all 
        finite successors of \((\gamma^+)^{N} = (\eta^{++})^{N}\).
    \end{proof}

body_md:
\label{lma:power_correct}
    In \(N\), if \(\alpha\geq \omega\)
    and \(\eta = \Theta(V_{\alpha+1})\),
    then for all \(\beta < \eta\), \(P(\beta) \subseteq \mathcal H(\eta^\omega)\).

        \(\textnormal{AD}_\mathbb R + \textnormal{DC}\).

        \(P(\beta)\subseteq L(\mathcal H|\bar \eta,I_{\bar \eta})\subseteq \mathcal H(\eta^\omega)\).
    \end{proof}

label: lma:V_vs_I
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lma:V_vs_I}
    In \(N\), for all \(\alpha\geq \omega\),
    \(|V_{\alpha}| =^* |I_\lambda|\)
    where \(\lambda = \sup_{\beta < \alpha} \Theta(V_\beta)\).
    \begin{proof}
        Work in \(N\). The nontrivial direction is
        \(|V_\alpha| \leq^* |I_\lambda|\).
        We produce the required surjections uniformly in \(\alpha\) by induction. 
        This uniformity handles the limit steps.
        For the successor step, 
        suppose \(|V_{\alpha}| \leq^* |I_\lambda|\), and let us show that \(|V_{\alpha+1}| \leq^* |\Theta(V_\alpha)^\omega|\).

        First, assume \(\textnormal{cf}(\alpha) = \omega\).
        Then \(|V_{\alpha+1}| =^* |V_\alpha^\omega| \leq^* |(I_\lambda)^\omega| =^* |\lambda^\omega|\leq^* |\Theta(V_\alpha)^\omega|\). 
        
        Otherwise, let \(\theta = \Theta(\lambda^\omega)\), and note that \(\theta \leq \Theta(V_\alpha)\) since \(|(V_\alpha)^\omega| = |V_\alpha|\).
        We use that 
        \(P(\lambda^\omega)\subseteq L_\theta(\mathcal H|\theta,I_\theta)\) by
        \cite[Theorems 10.6 and 10.13]{NairianModels}.
        Since every subset of \(V_\alpha\) can be coded by a subset of \(I_\lambda\),
        it follows that \(V_{\alpha+1}\subseteq L_\theta(\mathcal H|\theta,I_\theta)\).
        Thus \(|V_{\alpha+1}| \leq^* |I_\theta|\leq^* |I_{\Theta(V_\alpha)}|\), as desired.
    \end{proof}

\label{prp:strongs}
    The set of strong cardinals of \(\mathcal H\) is equal to
    \[S = \{\Theta(V_\alpha) : \alpha \geq \omega\text{ and }\alpha\in \xi\setminus S^\xi_\omega\}\]

        Fix \(\alpha\geq \omega\) and let
        \(\lambda = \sup_{\beta < \alpha} \Theta(V_\beta)\).
        We will show that the least strong of \(\mathcal H\) above \(\lambda\) is \(\min(S\setminus (\lambda+1))\).

        \(\Theta(V_{\alpha+1}) = \Theta(\lambda^\omega)\),
        and clearly \(\Theta(V_{\alpha+1}) = \min(S\setminus (\lambda+1))\). Otherwise,
        \(\Theta(V_\alpha) = \Theta(\lambda^\omega)\),
        and clearly \(\Theta(V_{\alpha}) = \min(S\setminus (\lambda+1))\).
    \end{proof}

label: thm:woodin_vopenka
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:woodin_vopenka}
    Suppose \(X\) is a transitive set and \(M\) is an inner model of \(\textnormal{ZFC}\) such that \(M = \textnormal{HOD}_{M\cup \{X\}}\).
    Let \(g \subseteq \textnormal{Col}(\omega,X)\) be \(V\)-generic and let \(\kappa = \Theta(X^{<\omega})\). Then
    \(g\) belongs to a \(\kappa\)-cc forcing extension of \(M\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We verify that
    \(M\) has the uniform \(\kappa\)-cover property in 
    \(M_g = \textnormal{HOD}^{V[g]}_{M\cup \{g\}}\) and then cite Bukovsky's criterion
    \cite[Proposition 4.37]{GoldbergUniqueness}.
    Suppose \(I\in M\) and \(f : I \to \textnormal{Ord}\) is a function in \(M_g\). Fix a formula \(\varphi\) and a parameter \(a\in M\) such that \[f(i) = \alpha\iff V[g]\vDash \varphi(i,\alpha,g,a)\]
    For each \(i\in I\), let 
    \[F(i) = \{\alpha\in \textnormal{Ord} : \exists p\in \textnormal{Col}(\omega,X)\, \left(p\Vdash \varphi(i,\alpha,g,a)\right)\}\]
    Then \(F\in M\), and for all \(i \in I\), \(f(i)\in F(i)\) and \(|F(i)| \leq^* |X^{<\omega}|\), so \(\textnormal{ot}(F(i)) < \kappa\).

label: prp:measurable-preserves-local-regularity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prp:measurable-preserves-local-regularity}
    Suppose \(\kappa\) is measurable and \(X\) is a transitive
    set with \(\Theta(X)\leq \kappa\). Then, for
    any inner model \(M\) of \(\textnormal{ZFC}\), the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item \(\kappa\) is strongly inaccessible in
        \(M(X)\).
        \item For any normal measure \(W\) on \(\kappa\),
        \(W\)-almost every \(\rho<\kappa\) remains regular in
        \(M(X)\).
    \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a measure \(W\) witnessing that \(\kappa\) is measurable.
    Let \(M'\) be the class of sets hereditarily
    ordinal definable from parameters in \(M\cup \{X,W\}\). Then \(M' = \textnormal{HOD}_{M'\cup \{X\}}\). Since \(M\subseteq M'\), it suffices to prove (1) and (2) for \(M'(X)\).

    Applying \cref{thm:woodin_vopenka},
    let \(\mathbb A\) be a \(\kappa\)-cc complete Boolean  
    algebra and \(G\subseteq \mathbb A\) be an \(M'\)-generic filter such that \(M'[G]\) contains a \(V\)-generic collapse \(g : \omega\to X\).
    Let \(\dot x\) be an \(\mathbb A\)-name for
    a real in \(M'[G]\) coding
    \(X\); for example, \(\dot x\) could code the pull-back
    of the membership relation \(\in\restriction X\) under \(\dot g\) to a binary relation on \(\omega\).
    Let \(\mathbb B\) be the complete subalgebra of 
    \(\mathbb A\) generated by the Boolean values of 
    \(\dot x(n) = m\) for \(n,m < \omega\).
    Then in \(M'\), \(\mathbb B\) is a countably generated \(\kappa\)-cc Boolean algebra and
    \(M'(X)\) is contained in a \(\mathbb B\)-generic extension of \(M'\).

    Since \(\kappa\) is measurable in \(M'\), \cref{lma:small-completely-generated-algebra} implies \(|\mathbb B| < \kappa\).
    Therefore \(\kappa\) remains strongly inaccessible in any \(\mathbb B\)-generic extension of \(M'\), and so \(\kappa\) is strongly inaccessible in 
    \(M'(X)\), which proves (1).
    For (2), note that if \(W\) is normal, then \(W\) concentrates on regular cardinals of \(M'\), and forcing with \(\mathbb B\) preserves all sufficiently large \(M'\)-regular cardinals below \(\kappa\).

label: cor:no-long-rank-sequences
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:no-long-rank-sequences}
    In \(N\), if \(\omega\leq \alpha < \xi\), there is no
    \(\Theta(V_\alpha)\)-sequence of distinct subsets of
    \(V_\alpha\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\kappa=\Theta(V_\alpha)\), which is measurable by
    \cref{thm:theta_meas}.

    First suppose that \(\alpha\) is a successor ordinal.
    Assume towards
    a contradiction that 
    \(\vec A=\langle A_\nu:\nu<\kappa\rangle\)
    is a sequence of distinct subsets of \(V_\alpha\).
    By \cref{lma:V_vs_I}, for some \(\eta<\kappa\),
    there is a surjection
    \(f:\eta^\omega\to V_\alpha\). (We can take
    \(\eta = \Theta(V_{\alpha-1})\).)
    Let
    \(B_\nu=f^{-1}[A_\nu]\) for \(\nu<\kappa\).
    Choose \(s\in I_\xi\) such that \(f\) and
    \(\vec A\) are \(\textnormal{OD}_s\). By
    \cite[Theorem 12.11]{FailureSquare}, the relation
    \[
        \{(\nu,t)\in\kappa\times\eta^\omega:t\in B_\nu\},
    \]
    has an \(\infty\)-Borel code in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\). Hence
    \(\langle B_\nu:\nu<\kappa\rangle\) belongs to
    \(\textnormal{HOD}_s(\eta^\omega)\).
    By \cref{prp:measurable-preserves-local-regularity}(1),
    \(\kappa\) is strongly inaccessible in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s(\eta^\omega)\),
    contradicting that
    \(\kappa\) injects into \(P(\eta^\omega)\)
    via the map \(f(\nu) = B_\nu\).

    Now suppose that \(\alpha\) is a limit ordinal, and let \(U\) be a nonprincipal
    \(\kappa\)-complete ultrafilter on \(\kappa\). 
    The successor case shows that if
    \(\beta<\alpha\), there is no
    \(\kappa\)-sequence of distinct subsets of \(V_\beta\).
    By \cite[Lemma 3.5]{Goldberg2024MeasurableChoiceless},
    \(U\) is therefore closed under
    \(V_\beta\)-indexed intersections. Since \(\alpha<\kappa\) and \(U\) is \(\kappa\)-complete, this implies that \(U\) is
    closed under \(V_\alpha\)-indexed intersections as well.
    A standard argument now
    shows that there is no \(\kappa\)-sequence of distinct subsets of \(V_\alpha\); see the proof of \cite[Lemma 10.4]{Jech2003SetTheory}.

label: thm:dichotomy
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dichotomy}
    Exactly one of the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item \label{item:eventual_complete} \(N\) satisfies
        that for all \(\kappa\), for all sufficiently large regular \(\delta\),
        \(W_\delta\) is \(\kappa\)-complete.
        \item \label{item:supercompact} \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\) satisfies that there is a supercompact cardinal.
    \end{enumerate}
    \begin{proof}
        Work in \(N^+\).
        Assume \ref{item:eventual_complete} fails. By \cref{thm:monotonicity},
        there is some cardinal \(\kappa_*\) such that for all sufficiently large
        regular \(\delta < \xi\), \(\kappa_\delta = \kappa_*\).
        
        By \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov} and \cref{prp:kappa_cov}, for all regular \(\delta \in [\kappa_*,\xi)\), 
        there is some \(s\in I_\xi\) such that
        \(\kappa_*\) is \(\delta\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\)
        and \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \(\kappa_*\)-cover 
        and approximation properties at \(\delta\).
        Let \(\gamma = \kappa_*^+\). 
        By the Hamkins uniqueness theorem \cite[Theorem 4.7]{Goldberg2024StronglyCompactOD},
        if \(M_0\) and \(M_1\) are inner models of ZFC with the
        \(\kappa_*\)-approximation and cover properties at \(\delta\)
        such that \(M_0\cap H(\gamma) = M_1\cap H(\gamma)\),
        then \(M_0 \cap P(\delta) = M_1\cap P(\delta)\).
        By a pigeonhole argument, using that \(\xi\) is inaccessible,
        we can find a single transitive model \(M\subseteq V_\xi\)
        with the \(\kappa_*\)-cover and approximation properties
        such that for arbitrarily large regular \(\delta\),
        there is some \(s\in I_\xi\)
        such that \(P(\delta)\cap M = P(\delta)\cap \textnormal{HOD}_s\)
        and \(\kappa_*\) is \(\delta\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\).

        It follows easily that \(\kappa_*\) is supercompact in \(M\)
        and \(M\) satisfies \(\textnormal{UA}\). Moreover
        \(M\) is ordinal definable from \(x = M\cap H(\gamma)\).
        Thus \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_x\). 
        Note also that \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\) has the \(\kappa_*\)-cover and approximation properties in \(M\) 
        since \(M\vDash \textnormal{UA}\) and \(\textnormal{UA}\) implies that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) is a weak extender
        model at each supercompact cardinal \cite[Theorem 6.2.15]{UABook}.

        We now leave \(N^+\) and work in the ambient determinacy model. 
        We have that \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_x^{N^+}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_x\).
        By Vop\v{e}nka's theorem, \(\textnormal{HOD}_x\) is contained in a \(\rho\)-cc
        generic extension of \(\textnormal{HOD}\) for some \(\rho < \xi\). 
        (A coarse upper bound is \(\rho = (\Theta(V_{\gamma+1}))^N\).)
        Since \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\) has the \(\kappa_*\)-cover property below \(\xi\) 
        and is contained in a \(\rho\)-cc generic extension of \(\textnormal{HOD}\), it follows that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) has the
        \((\kappa_*,\rho)\)-cover property below \(\xi\). This covering property
        implies that for all regular \(\delta\in (\rho,\xi)\), \(\textnormal{HOD}\) satisfies
        \(\kappa_{\mathscr K_\delta}\leq \rho\). Applying \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov},
        it follows immediately that there is a supercompact cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\).

        Finally, we sketch the proof that \ref{item:eventual_complete} and \ref{item:supercompact}
        are mutually exclusive. Assume \ref{item:supercompact} holds.
        We will show that \(\xi\) is a limit of regular cardinals in \(N^+\).
        Granting this, let us show that \ref{item:eventual_complete} fails. 
        Let \(\kappa_0\) be the least supercompact of \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\). 
        By \cite[Lemma 7.4.49]{UABook} if \(\kappa_0\leq \delta < \xi\) and \(\delta\) is a regular cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}\),
        then \(\mathscr K_\delta^0 = (\mathscr K_\delta)^\textnormal{HOD}\) has completeness
        \(\kappa_0\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}\).
        If \(\delta > \kappa_0\) is regular in \(N\), then by \cref{prp:W_to_K}
        \(\kappa_\delta\leq \kappa_{\mathscr K_\delta^0} = \kappa_0\), which rules out \ref{item:eventual_complete}.
        
        We now show that \(\xi\) is a limit of regular cardinals in \(N^+\).
        First, note that \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov} shows that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa_0)\)-cover
        property below \(\xi\). 
        Thus the same is true for \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) for any \(s\in I_\xi\),
        and it follows from \cref{lma:ketonen} that 
        there is a supercompact cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\xi\).
        Let us denote by \(\kappa_s\) the least supercompact cardinal of \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\xi\). 
        Thus \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa_s)\)-cover property below \(\xi\).

        Fix \(s\in I_\xi\) with \(\kappa_s\) as small as possible.
        We claim that \(\kappa_s\) is regular in \(N\):
        otherwise, take \(t\in I_\xi\) such that \(s\in \textnormal{HOD}_t\) and
        \(\kappa_s\) is singular in \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\). Since \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_t\), 
        \(\kappa_t\leq \kappa_s\), but since \(\kappa_s\) is singular
        in \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\), \(\kappa_t < \kappa_s\), contrary to the minimality of \(\kappa_s\).
        The proof of \cite[Theorem 2.8]{Goldberg2024StronglyCompactOD} 
        now shows that if \(\kappa_s \leq \delta < \xi\) and \(\delta\) is regular in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\),
        then in \(N\), \(\textnormal{cf}(\delta) = |\delta|\). 
        Since \(\xi\) is a limit cardinal in \(N^+\),
        it follows that \(\xi\) is a limit of regular cardinals.
    \end{proof}

        since \(M\vDash \textnormal{UA}\) and \(\textnormal{UA}\) implies that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) is a weak extender
        model at each supercompact cardinal \cite[Theorem 6.2.15]{UABook}.

        We now leave \(N^+\) and work in the ambient determinacy model. 
        We have that \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_x^{N^+}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_x\).
        By Vop\v{e}nka's theorem, \(\textnormal{HOD}_x\) is contained in a \(\rho\)-cc
        generic extension of \(\textnormal{HOD}\) for some \(\rho < \xi\). 
        (A coarse upper bound is \(\rho = (\Theta(V_{\gamma+1}))^N\).)
        Since \(\textnormal{HOD}^M\) has the \(\kappa_*\)-cover property below \(\xi\) 
        and is contained in a \(\rho\)-cc generic extension of \(\textnormal{HOD}\), it follows that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) has the
        \((\kappa_*,\rho)\)-cover property below \(\xi\). This covering property
        implies that for all regular \(\delta\in (\rho,\xi)\), \(\textnormal{HOD}\) satisfies
        \(\kappa_{\mathscr K_\delta}\leq \rho\). Applying \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov},
        it follows immediately that there is a supercompact cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\).

        Finally, we sketch the proof that \ref{item:eventual_complete} and \ref{item:supercompact}
        are mutually exclusive. Assume \ref{item:supercompact} holds.
        We will show that \(\xi\) is a limit of regular cardinals in \(N^+\).
        Granting this, let us show that \ref{item:eventual_complete} fails. 
        Let \(\kappa_0\) be the least supercompact of \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\). 
        By \cite[Lemma 7.4.49]{UABook} if \(\kappa_0\leq \delta < \xi\) and \(\delta\) is a regular cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}\),
        then \(\mathscr K_\delta^0 = (\mathscr K_\delta)^\textnormal{HOD}\) has completeness
        \(\kappa_0\) in \(\textnormal{HOD}\).
        If \(\delta > \kappa_0\) is regular in \(N\), then by \cref{prp:W_to_K}
        \(\kappa_\delta\leq \kappa_{\mathscr K_\delta^0} = \kappa_0\), which rules out \ref{item:eventual_complete}.
        
        We now show that \(\xi\) is a limit of regular cardinals in \(N^+\).
        First, note that \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov} shows that \(\textnormal{HOD}\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa_0)\)-cover
        property below \(\xi\). 
        Thus the same is true for \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) for any \(s\in I_\xi\),
        and it follows from \cref{lma:ketonen} that 
        there is a supercompact cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\xi\).
        Let us denote by \(\kappa_s\) the least supercompact cardinal of \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\cap V_\xi\). 
        Thus \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa_s)\)-cover property below \(\xi\).

        Fix \(s\in I_\xi\) with \(\kappa_s\) as small as possible.
        We claim that \(\kappa_s\) is regular in \(N\):
        otherwise, take \(t\in I_\xi\) such that \(s\in \textnormal{HOD}_t\) and
        \(\kappa_s\) is singular in \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\). Since \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}_t\), 
        \(\kappa_t\leq \kappa_s\), but since \(\kappa_s\) is singular
        in \(\textnormal{HOD}_t\), \(\kappa_t < \kappa_s\), contrary to the minimality of \(\kappa_s\).
        The proof of \cite[Theorem 2.8]{Goldberg2024StronglyCompactOD} 
        now shows that if \(\kappa_s \leq \delta < \xi\) and \(\delta\) is regular in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\),
        then in \(N\), \(\textnormal{cf}(\delta) = |\delta|\). 
        Since \(\xi\) is a limit cardinal in \(N^+\),
        it follows that \(\xi\) is a limit of regular cardinals.

\label{conj:ssh}
    Assume \(\textnormal{AD}^+ + V = L(P(\mathbb R))\). 
    Suppose \(\gamma < \Theta\) and the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item \(\gamma\) is a cardinal in \(\textnormal{HOD}\).
        \item No ordinal \(\kappa < \gamma\) is \({<}\gamma\)-supercompact in \(\textnormal{HOD}\).
        \item \(\textnormal{cf}(\gamma) = \omega\).

label: prp:not_vacuous
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prp:not_vacuous}
    Assume \cref{conj:ssh}. If \(\xi\) is inaccessible in \(\textnormal{HOD}\)
    and \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\) satisfies that there is a supercompact cardinal,
    then \(\xi\) is inaccessible in \(N^+\).
    \begin{proof}
        Let \(\kappa\) be the least supercompact cardinal of \(\textnormal{HOD}\cap V_\xi\).
        We begin by computing \(\Theta_0(\kappa^\omega)\).
        Note that \(\kappa\) is a limit of cardinals \(\gamma\) satisfying
        the hypotheses of \cref{conj:ssh}. 
        Since \(\kappa\) is a limit of Woodins in \(\textnormal{HOD}\), 
        this implies that \(\Theta_0(\gamma^\omega) < \kappa\) for all \(\gamma < \kappa\). 
        Moreover by the \(\textnormal{HOD}\)-ultrafilter hypothesis (\cref{thm:hod_uf}), \(\textnormal{cf}(\kappa)\geq \omega_1\).
        Therefore \(\Theta_0(\kappa^\omega) = \kappa^{+\textnormal{HOD}}\).
        
        Let \(\mathbb P\in \textnormal{HOD}\) be the product Vop\v{e}nka forcing adding a sequence of elements of
        \(\kappa^\omega\) to \(\textnormal{HOD}\).
        By counting ordinal definable \(\infty\)-Borel codes, 
        one can show \(\textnormal{HOD}\vDash |\mathbb P| \leq 2^{<\theta}\) where \(\theta = \Theta_0(\kappa^\omega)\).
        In particular, \(|\mathbb P| < \xi\). 
        Since \(\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa^\omega}\) is an inner model of a \(\mathbb P\)-generic extension of
        \(\textnormal{HOD}\), it follows that \(\xi\) remains inaccessible in \(\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa^\omega}\).

        By \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov}, \(\textnormal{HOD}\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa)\)-cover property
        below \(\xi\). Therefore \(N^+ = \textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa^\omega}\),
        and so \(\xi\) remains inaccessible in \(N^+\), proving the proposition.
    \end{proof}

label: thm:abn
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abn}
    Suppose that there is a class function that assigns
    to each regular cardinal \(\delta\) a uniform measure \(U_\delta\in \textnormal{meas}(\delta)\) so that
    the function \(\delta \mapsto \kappa_{U_\delta}\) is monotone and unbounded. 
    Then there is a class symmetric extension
    satisfying \(\textnormal{ZF}\) in which every uncountable cardinal is singular.
    \begin{proof}
        We may assume there is a proper class of regular cardinals.
        Let \[C = \{\gamma \in \textnormal{Ord} : |\{\kappa_{U_\delta}: \delta\in \textnormal{Reg}\cap \gamma\}| = \gamma\}\]
        and let \(\langle \kappa_i : i \in \textnormal{Ord}\rangle\) enumerate the Beth fixed-points in \(C\) in increasing order.
        (An ordinal \(\kappa\) is a \textit{Beth fixed-point}
        if for all \(a\in V_\kappa\), \(\Theta(a) < \kappa\).)
        Let \(\vec U = \langle U_\delta: \delta\in \textnormal{Reg}\rangle\). 
        Let \(\mathbb P = \mathbb P_\text{fin}(\vec U)\) be Adkisson--Ben-Neria's class forcing 
        from \cite[Definition 56]{AdkissonBenNeria2025}.
        The proofs of \cite[Lemma 57 and Proposition 64]{AdkissonBenNeria2025},
        showing that Adkisson--Ben-Neria's symmetric submodel of \(V^\mathbb P\) 
        satisfies \(\textnormal{ZF}\) plus all uncountable cardinals are singular, 
        ostensibly require the existence of a rank Berkeley cardinal.
        In fact, their proofs go through in our context, with 
        the sequence of almost supercompact cardinals replaced by 
        the sequence \(\langle \kappa_i : i \in \textnormal{Ord}\rangle\) defined above. 
    \end{proof}

name: Spector

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose \(H\in \textnormal{HOD}\) is a countable transitive model 
        of \(\textnormal{ZF}\) admitting an elementary embedding \(\rho : H \to \mathscr H\)
        with \(\xi\in \textnormal{ran}(\rho)\), and let \(\bar \xi = \rho^{-1}(\xi)\). Applying
        \(\textnormal{AD}_\mathbb R\), let \(\gamma \in (\xi,\Theta)\) be least such that
        every \(s\in I_\xi\) is \({<}\gamma\)-generic over \(\textnormal{HOD}\),
        and let \(\bar \gamma = \rho^{-1}(\gamma)\).

        We will use the construction from \cref{thm:ua}.
        Let \(\tilde{M}\) denote the model \(M\) from 
        \cref{thm:derived2}, and let
        \(M = \rho^{-1}[\tilde{M}]\).
        Let \(D\) be a derived model of \(M\) at the 
        appropriate limit of Woodin cardinals and let
        \(i : H \to \mathscr H^D\) be the embedding
        corresponding to the one from \cref{thm:derived2}.
        We may assume that \(i\restriction \bar \gamma\in M\cap D\).
        In particular, \(M\cap P(\bar \gamma) = H\cap P(\bar \gamma)\).

        Suppose \(\bar{\mathcal N}\in \textnormal{HOD}\) is an outer model of
        \(H\) such that \(\rho\) is partial elementary from
        \((\bar{\mathcal N},H)\) to \((N^+,\mathscr H)\).
        Let \(\bar I = I_{\bar \xi}\cap \bar{\mathcal N}\).
        By our choice of \(\bar \gamma\), every
        \(s\in \bar I\) is \({<}\bar\gamma\)-generic over
        \(H\), and since \(M\cap P(\bar \gamma) = H\cap P(\bar \gamma)\),
        it follows that the same is true for \(M\).

        Let \(\mathbb R^* = \mathbb R\cap \tilde{M}\), and
        as in \cref{thm:ua},
        let \(\pi : M \to M^*\) be a Neeman-style \(\mathbb R^*\)-genericity
        iteration with critical point above \(\bar \gamma\). 
        Let \(D^*\) be the derived model of \(M^*\) computed in
        \(M^*(\mathbb R^*)\), and recall as in 
        \cref{thm:ua} that \(P(\mathbb R^*)\cap D^* \unlhd \textnormal{Hom}^{\tilde{M}}\). 
        
        Note that \(k = \pi \circ i\) is an elementary embedding
        from \(H\) to \(H^* = \mathscr H^{D^*}\).
        Moreover, since
        \(i\restriction \bar \xi\in M\cap D\) and \(\textnormal{crit}(\pi) > \bar \xi\),
        we have \(k\restriction \bar\xi = 
        \pi(i\restriction \bar\xi) \in D^*\).
        We claim that \(k\) lifts to an elementary embedding
        \[\hat{k} : (\bar{\mathcal N},H)\to (\mathcal N^*,H^*)\]
        where \(\mathcal N^* = (N_{k(\bar \xi)}^+)^{D^*}\).
        Namely, if \(a\in \bar{\mathcal N}\) is definable in 
        \((\bar{\mathcal N},H)\) from \(s\in \bar I\), set \(\hat{k}(a)\) 
        equal to the element of \(\mathcal N^*\) defined 
        in \((\mathcal N^*,H^*)\) from \(k[s]\) in the same way.
        Note here that \(k[s]\in D^*\) since \(k\restriction \bar\xi\in D^*\).
        The fact that \(\hat{k}\) is well-defined and elementary follows from
        the fact that \(\pi\circ i\) extends, for each \(s\in \bar I\),
        to an elementary embedding from \(H_s\) to \(\mathscr H^{D^*}_{k[s]}\),
        using \cref{thm:derived2} and the fact that \(\textnormal{crit}(\pi) > \bar\gamma\).

        Since it will be relevant in \cref{thm:ua_N},
        we note that the embedding \(\hat k\) is close to \(\bar{\mathcal N}\). Fix ordinals \(\delta\) and \(\alpha < k(\delta)\), and let
        \(U\) be the \(\bar{\mathcal N}\)-measure on \(\delta\) derived from \(\hat{k}\) using \(\alpha\).
        Let 
        \(\tilde{U}\) be the \(M\)-ultrafilter on \(i(\delta)\) derived from \(\pi\) using \(\alpha\). 
        Since \(\pi\) is close to \(M\), \(\tilde{U}\in M\). Moreover, since \(\textnormal{crit}(\pi) > \bar\gamma\), \(\kappa_{\tilde{U}} > \bar\gamma\),
        and therefore for each \(s\in \bar I\), Levy--Solovay implies
        \(\tilde{U}\) generates a measure \(\tilde{U}_s\) 
        in \(M[s] = M[i[s]]\).
        Finally, \[U = \{A\in P(\delta)\cap \bar{\mathcal N} : \exists s\in \bar I\, (A\in H[s]\wedge i_s(A)\in \tilde{U}_s)\}\]
        and this is definable over 
        \((\bar{\mathcal N},H)\) from the parameter 
        \(\tilde{U}\in M\subseteq H\).

        Now fix a finitely generated structure \(H\)
        with an elementary \(\rho : H \to \mathscr H\)
        such that \(\rho(\bar \xi) = \xi\) and \(\rho(\bar \Theta) = \Theta\).
        Construct \(\bar {V}\in \textnormal{HOD}\) by a type omission argument
        so that \(H = \mathscr H^{\bar {V}}\).
        Let \(\bar{\mathcal N} = (N_{\bar \xi}^+)^{\bar V}\).

        Suppose that \(X,\mathcal U\in \bar{\mathcal N}\) and \(\bar{\mathcal N}\)
        satisfies that \(\mathcal U\) is
        a normal measure on \(P_{\omega_1}(X)\). 
        We will show that \(\mathcal U\) is the measure derived from
        the embedding \(\hat{k} : \bar{\mathcal N}\to \mathcal N^*\)
        defined above using \(\hat{k}[X]\).

        Using Spector's ultrapower construction, form in \(\textnormal{HOD}\)
        an elementary \(j : \bar{\mathcal N}\to \mathcal P\)
        such that \(\mathcal U\) is the measure
        derived from \(j\) using \(j[X]\) and \(j\restriction (P(\textnormal{Ord})\cap \bar{\mathcal N})\)
        agrees with the ultrapower embedding of \(\mathcal U\).
        Let \(H_{\mathcal P} = j(H)\). 
        By a standard realizability argument, there is an elementary embedding
        \(\rho_{\mathcal P} : H_{\mathcal P}\to \mathscr H\)
        such that \(\rho = \rho_{\mathcal P}\circ j\restriction H\).
        This embedding is automatically partial elementary from \(\mathcal P\) to \(N^+\) since the first-order theory of \(N^+\) with ordinal parameters uniformly reduces to that of \(\mathscr H\).

        Applying the construction above to \(\mathcal P\) instead of \(\bar{\mathcal N}\),
        we obtain \(\hat{k}_{\mathcal P} : \mathcal P \to \mathcal N^*_{\mathcal P}\).
        Using that \(H\) is finitely generated, one 
        can show as in \cref{thm:ua} that the relevant derived models are equal.
        Moreover,
        \(\hat{k}\restriction H = \hat{k}_{\mathcal P}\circ j\restriction H\) since \(H\) is finitely generated
        and these are close embeddings. 
        We can now conclude that \(\mathcal N^*_{\mathcal P} = \mathcal N^*\). 
        Moreover, it follows that
        \(\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{k}_{\mathcal P}\circ j\) agree on \(\bar I\), and hence on \(\bar{\mathcal N}\).
        In particular, \(\hat{k}_{\mathcal P}(j[X]) = \hat{k}_{\mathcal P}\circ j[X] = \hat{k}[X]\).
        Since \(\mathcal U\) is derived from \(j\) using \(j[X]\), we also have that
        \(\mathcal U\) is derived from \(\hat{k}_{\mathcal P}\circ j\) using \(\hat{k}_{\mathcal P}(j[X])\). 
        In other words, \(\mathcal U\) is the measure derived from \(\hat{k}\) using \(\hat{k}[X]\).

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lma:nt_inacc}
    If \(\delta\) is an NT-cardinal, then \(\delta\) is regular
    and \(\delta\) is inaccessible in any inner model of \(\textnormal{ZFC}\).
    \begin{proof}
        Fix \(\alpha\) such that \(\delta = \Theta(V_\alpha)\).
        By \(\textnormal{DC}\), \(\delta\) has uncountable cofinality.
        To see \(\delta\) is regular, note that combining the final two clauses of the definition of an NT-cardinal, one obtains that 
        for all sufficiently large ordinals \(\theta\), for any \(\gamma < \delta\) and \(a\in V_\theta\), there is some \(X\preceq V_{\theta+1}\) with \(\gamma\cup\{a\}\subseteq X\) and \(|X| \leq^* |V_\alpha|\). An argument similar to \cref{lma:limit-successor-regular} from \cref{thm:theta_meas} then implies \(\delta\) is regular.

        Now to see \(\delta\) is inaccessible in any inner model \(M\) of ZFC, we just need to show \(\delta\) is a strong limit cardinal in \(M\). For any \(\rho < \delta\), \(|\rho|\leq^* |V_\alpha|\), and so \(|P(\rho)|\leq |V_{\alpha+1}|\), which implies \(|P(\rho)\cap M| < \aleph(V_{\alpha+1}) = \delta\).
        Thus \((2^\rho)^M < |P(\rho)\cap M|^+\leq \delta\). 
    \end{proof}

        belongs to \(\mathcal H_{s,x}\) for some \(x\subseteq \kappa\).

        \(\mathcal H_{s,x}\) is a 
        \(\delta\)-cc generic extension of \(\mathcal H_s\) for each \(x\subseteq \kappa\).

        \(P(\kappa) = \bigcup_{\beta< \delta}S_\beta\)
        with \(|S_\beta|\leq^* |V_\alpha|\).

        implies \(\mathcal H_{s,x}\) is a \(\delta\)-cc
        generic extension of \(\mathcal H_s\).

        \(\mathcal H_s\) correctly computes all finite successors of \(\delta\) and \(\kappa\) is \({<}\delta^{+\omega}\)-supercompact in \(\mathcal H_t\) for all \(t\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\) such that \(\mathcal H_s\subseteq \mathcal H_t\). 

        We claim that \(\Theta(P(\delta)) \leq \delta^{++}\).
        Fix a surjection \(f : P(\delta)\to \eta\), and let us show that \(\eta < \delta^{++}\).

        \(\Theta(P(\kappa))\leq \delta^+\)
        since \(P(\kappa) = \bigcup_{\beta< \delta}S_\beta\)
        where \(|S_\beta|\leq^* |V_\alpha|\).

        where \(Y_a = P(\delta)\cap \mathcal H_{s,a}\).

        \(\mathcal H_{s,a}\subseteq \mathcal H_t\); since
        \(\mathcal H_t\) satisfies \(\textnormal{UA}\) plus
        \(\kappa\) is \({<}\delta^{+\omega}\)-supercompact,
        we have \(2^\delta = \delta^+\) in \(\mathcal H_t\) by \cite{UAGCH}; since \(\mathcal H_{s,a}\) is cardinal correct in the interval \([\delta,\delta^{+\omega})\), we obtain \(2^\delta = \delta^+\) in \(\mathcal H_{s,a}\).
        Thus using the canonical well-order of \(\mathcal H_{s,a}\), we can fix bijections \(g_a : \delta^+\to Y_a\).
        Now if \(f : P(\delta)\to \eta\),
        then 
        \[\eta = \bigcup_{a\in P(\kappa)} f[Y_a] = \bigcup_{a\in P(\kappa)} (f\circ g_a)[\delta^+]\]
        It follows that \(|\eta|\leq^* |P(\kappa)\times \delta^+|\), and using \(\Theta(P(\kappa)) \leq \delta^+\), we obtain that \(\eta < \delta^{++}\).

        Applying the Hamkins uniqueness theorem as in \cref{thm:main}, it follows that
        every bounded subset of \(\delta^{+\omega}\) belongs to
        a \(\delta^{++}\)-cc extension of \(\mathcal H\), and
        therefore \(\mathcal H\) correctly computes all finite successors of \(\delta^{++}\).
    \end{proof}

title: Definition
body_md:
If \(U\) is an ultrafilter on \(X\) and \(P\) and \(Q\) are partitions of \(X\),
then \textit{\(P\) refines \(Q\) modulo \(U\)}, denoted \(P\leq_U Q\), 
if there is some \(A\in U\)
such that \(P\restriction A\) refines \(Q\restriction A\).

We say \(U\) is \textit{\(\gamma\)-decomposable} if there is a
partition \(P\) of \(X\) such that \(|P| = \gamma\) and 
whenever \(Q\leq_U P\),
\(|Q| \geq \gamma\). The \textit{decomposability spectrum} \(D(U)\) consists of all \(\gamma\)
such that \(U\) is \(\gamma\)-decomposable.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lma:limit_spectrum}
    Suppose \(\gamma\) is a strong limit cardinal of countable cofinality or a limit of such cardinals. If there is a measure \(U\) on an ordinal
    with \(\sup(D(U)\cap \gamma) = \gamma\), then \(\mathcal H\) correctly computes all finite successors of \(\gamma\).
    \begin{proof}
        First assume \(\textnormal{cf}(\gamma) = \omega\). 
        Let \(\eta\) be the underlying ordinal of \(U\) and pick 
        \(\gamma_n\in D(U)\) increasing to \(\gamma\) and functions
        \(f_n : \eta\to \gamma_n\) witnessing \(\gamma_n\in D(U)\).
        Fix \(s\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\) such that \((f_n)_{n < \omega}\in \mathcal H_s\).
        Thus in \(\mathcal H_s\), 
        \(\textnormal{cf}(\gamma) = \omega\) and \(\gamma = \sup (D(\bar U)\cap \gamma)\)
        where \(\bar U = U\cap \mathcal H_s\). 
        The proof of \cite[Lemma 5.4]{GoldbergUniqueness} shows that
        in \(\textnormal{HOD}_s\), there is a countably complete uniform ultrafilter
        on \(\delta = (\gamma^+)^{ \mathcal H_s}\). 
        Therefore by \cite[Corollary 7.4.10]{UABook}
        some ordinal \(\kappa < \gamma\) is 
        \(\delta\)-supercompact in \( \mathcal H_s\). 
        The proof of \cite[Lemma 5.4]{GoldbergUniqueness} shows moreover that \(\delta = \gamma^+\): let
        \[X = \{\langle f_n(\xi) : {n < \omega}\rangle : \xi < \eta\}\] and note that \(X\in \mathcal H_s\), \(X\subseteq \gamma^\omega\), and \(|X| \geq \gamma^+\); therefore using Solovay's theorem on the SCH above strongly compact cardinals, \[\delta = (\gamma^+)^{ \mathcal H_s} = (\gamma^\omega)^{\mathcal H_s}\geq \gamma^+\] It follows that \(\delta\) is regular and
        \(\kappa_{\delta} < \delta\). By \cref{lma:hod_transfer},
        \(\mathcal H\) correctly computes all finite
        successors of \(\gamma\).

        We now consider the case where \(\gamma\) has uncountable cofinality. The previous case implies that there is an \(\omega\)-club \(C\) of cardinals \(\bar \gamma < \gamma\)
        such that \((\bar \gamma^+)^{\mathcal H} = \bar\gamma^+\).

        If \(\gamma\) is singular, then a Silver-style argument establishes
        that \((\gamma^{+})^{\mathcal H} = \gamma^+\).
        Namely, let \(\iota = \textnormal{cf}(\gamma)\), and let
        \(j : V \to M\) be the Spector ultrapower via \(W_\iota\).
        Note that \(\sup j[\gamma] = \gamma\) since \(\gamma\) is a strong limit, and hence \(\gamma\in j(C)\).
        Also \((\gamma^{+})^M\geq \gamma^+\): if \(\preceq\) is a well-order of \(\gamma\), then \({\preceq}^* = j({\preceq})\restriction \gamma\) is a well-order of \(\gamma\) that belongs to \(M\) with \(\textnormal{ot}({\preceq}^*)\) at least \(\textnormal{ot}({\preceq})\).
        This implies
        \[(\gamma^+)^{\mathcal H} \geq (\gamma^+)^{j(\mathcal H)} \geq (\gamma^+)^M \geq \gamma^+\]
        Thus \(\gamma^+\) is regular and we can apply \cref{lma:hod_transfer} to \(\delta = \gamma^+\);
        note that \(\kappa_{\gamma^+} < \gamma\) since 
        \(\kappa_{\gamma^+}\) is regular.

        If \(\gamma\) is regular, we can apply \cref{lma:hod_transfer}
        directly to \(\delta = \gamma\) once we show that
        \(\kappa_\gamma < \gamma\).
        Assume towards a contradiction that \(\kappa_{W_\gamma} = \gamma\). 
        Note that for a \(W_\gamma\)-large set of \(\bar \gamma\),
        \(\mathcal H\) correctly computes \(\bar\gamma^+\) and hence \(\mathcal H\) 
        satisfies that some \(\kappa < \bar \gamma\) is
        \(\bar \gamma^+\)-supercompact.
        Since \(W_\gamma\) is normal, 
        there is a fixed \(\kappa < \gamma\) that is \({<}\gamma\)-supercompact in \(\mathcal H\). By \cref{prp:gamma_kappa_cov}, it follows that \(\mathcal H\) has the \((\aleph_1,\kappa)\)-cover property at \(\gamma\),
        and by \cref{lma:ketonen},
        it follows that \((\kappa_{\mathscr K_\gamma})^{\mathcal H}\leq \kappa < \gamma\). By \cref{cor:ua_completeness}, this contradicts that \(\kappa_\gamma = \gamma\). 
    \end{proof}

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lma:NT_spectrum}
    Suppose \(\delta\) is an NT-cardinal, \(U\) is a measure on an ordinal, and one of the following holds: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \(\sup (D(U)\cap \theta) < \delta\) where \(\theta = \aleph(P(\delta))\).
        \item \(\mathcal H\) does not correctly compute all finite successors of \(\delta^{++}\).
    \end{itemize}
    Then \(U\) has a finest partition below \(\delta\).
    \begin{proof}
        Fix \(\alpha\) such that \(\delta = \Theta(V_\alpha)\). 
        Fix \(\theta\) sufficiently large and take a \(V_\alpha\)-closed \(X\preceq V_{\theta+1}\) with \(|X| \leq^* |V_{\alpha+1}|\) containing the finitely many relevant parameters. Write 
        \[X = \bigcup_{\beta < \delta} X_\beta\] where \(|X_\beta| \leq^* |V_\alpha|\). Note that each \(X_\beta\in X\) by \(V_\alpha\)-closure. 
        Let \(\eta\) be the underlying ordinal of \(U\) and for \(\beta < \delta\), define a partition \(P_\beta\) of \(\eta\) by putting \(\xi_0,\xi_1 < \eta\) into the same cell if and only if \(D(X_\beta,\xi_0) = D(X_\beta,\xi_1)\) where \[D(X_\beta,\xi) = \{A\in P(\eta)\cap X_\beta: \xi\in A\}\] 
        Then \(P_\beta\in X\) since \(X_\beta\in X\).
        Moreover, we claim that \(|P_\beta| < \delta\). 
        First, note that \(P_\beta\) injects into \(P(X_\beta)\):
        map a cell \(B\in P_\beta\) to the common value
        of \(D(X_\beta,\xi)\) for all \(\xi\in B\).
        Since \(P_\beta\) is well-orderable, 
        \[|P_\beta| < \aleph(P(X_\beta)) \leq \aleph(V_{\alpha+1}) = \delta\]

        To show \(U\) has a finest partition, it suffices to show that this sequence stabilizes modulo \(U\), or in other words that there is some \(\beta < \delta\) such that for all \(\beta'\geq \beta\), \(P_\beta \equiv P_{\beta'}\). 
        Then since \(P_\beta\in X\), \(P_\beta\) is a finest partition of \(U\) below \(\delta\).

        Assume first that \(\sup(D(U)\cap \theta) < \delta\) where \(\theta = \aleph(P(\delta))\). Let \(Q\) be the least common refinement of \((P_\beta)_{\beta < \delta}\). Note that \(|Q|\leq |P(\delta)|\). Since \(Q\) is well-orderable, 
        \(|Q| < \aleph(P(\delta))\). Since \(\sup(D(U)\cap \theta) < \delta\), there is some \(A\in U\) such that \(|Q\restriction A| < \delta\).
        Thus there is then some \(\beta < \delta\) such that for all \(\beta'\geq \beta\), \(P_\beta\restriction A = P_{\beta'} \restriction A\). 
        Since \(P_\beta\in X\), \(P_\beta\) is a finest partition of \(U\) below \(\delta\).

        We finish by proving \(U\) has a finest partition below \(\delta\) in the case that \(\mathcal H\) does not correctly compute all finite successors of \(\delta^{++}\).
        Take \(s\in \textnormal{Ord}^\omega\) such that
        \(\langle P_\beta : \beta < \delta\rangle\in \mathcal H_s\).
        Let \(\bar U = U\cap \mathcal H_s\) and let \(\mu = \sup (D(\bar U)\cap \delta)\). If \(\mu < \delta\), then since \(\delta\) is inaccessible in \(\mathcal H_s\), the sequence \((P_\beta)_{\beta < \delta}\) stabilizes modulo \(U\): there cannot be a strictly Rudin--Keisler increasing \(\delta\)-sequence of measures on \(\mu\).

        So assume towards a contradiction that
        \(\mu = \delta\).
        Then some \(\kappa < \delta\) is \(\delta\)-supercompact 
        in \(\mathcal H_s\). 
        It follows from \cref{cor:ua_completeness} that \(\kappa_\delta < \delta\),
        and so by \cref{lma:hod_transfer}, \(\mathcal H\) correctly
        computes all finite successors of \(\delta^{++}\).
    \end{proof}

    successors of \(\lambda^{++}\). 
    Let \(F\) be a \(\lambda\)-complete filter on an ordinal
    \(\eta\). Let \(U\) be the Ketonen least measure on \(\eta\)
